title: Soft repair with two functional dependencies sharing a left-hand side
description:
This note resolves the exact soft-repair complexity of the fixed schema R(A,B,C) with separately penalized A→B and A→C. The case is the first open dependency set in Carmeli, Grohe, Kimelfeld, Livshits and Tibi's 2024 ACM TODS article, also listed in the 2021 ICDT version. Threshold decision is NP-complete and exact optimization is NP-hard. Hardness holds when all facts share one A value and one positive integer deletion weight, and the A→C penalty is one.

The reduction creates one equal-size B block per graph vertex. For each edge, its endpoints share one C label. The large finite A→B penalty and common deletion weight make every optimum select exactly k full blocks. At a fixed retained size, packing minimizes cross-block B violations; the primary score peaks when exactly k blocks are full. The number of remaining equal C pairs then matches the count of edges induced by the chosen vertices. An optimum reaches the clique threshold exactly when the chosen blocks form a clique.

Retained pairs are evaluated separately for each dependency, and a pair violating both pays both costs. Their conjunction is equivalent to A→BC under hard constraints, but a single soft A→BC penalty charges a different objective. The source's single-dependency, soft matching and hard-repair results therefore do not give this classification. Numerical penalties are input and are polynomially bounded integers in the reduction; the all-fixed-weights problem remains outside the theorem.

The release includes the manuscript, LaTeX, bibliography, citation metadata, checksum ledger and complete evidence archive. The standard-library replay checks 285 small graph/target cases and 105,252 retained-subset scores, with an independent pairwise calculation of the 256 repairs of the worked example. Its triangle costs 2,828, while a nonclique choice of three full blocks costs 2,830. The rotating figure and offline explorer expose every subset's costs. External peer review and formal verification are pending.

ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the recovered proof and original replay under human direction. OpenAI Codex independently reviewed the mathematics. GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI) checked primary sources and prepared the manuscript, extended replay and illustration. DannyExperiments is the project citation identity.
